queue.add_to_queue_title: Adds these files to each printer's queue. Idle printers pick them up automatically; busy printers keep them queued until they're free.
queue.send_button_title: Starts eligible idle printers immediately. Jobs for busy printers remain queued.

queue.recovery_required_title: Queue data could not be recovered
queue.recovery_required_body: Both the queue state file and its backup were unreadable. All queue automation is paused, and the damaged files have been kept for inspection rather than discarded. This can't be undone — resetting starts every printer's queue empty.
queue.store_degraded_line: Queue state is not currently durable — automatic retry in progress.
queue.store_stopped_by_admin_line: Queue automation was manually stopped for every printer.
queue.delete_pool_confirm: Delete pool "{name}"? Printers must be reassigned first if any are still using it.
queue.attention_detail_recovery_mismatch: Printer is printing a file SnapCon didn't dispatch: {filename}
queue.no_pools_assigned: No printers are assigned to a Printer Pool yet — assign one from Settings → Printers.
queue.release_error_confirm: Release this printer from its error state? This ejects the currently loaded file.
queue.stop_queue_confirm: Stop this printer's queue? Nothing further will start automatically until you resume it — the current print, if any, keeps running.
queue.clear_queue_confirm: Clear this printer's entire queue? If it's currently printing, that print is cancelled immediately and any progress is lost. Every other queued item is removed too. This can't be undone.
queue.cancel_print_confirm: Cancel the current print on this printer? This stops it immediately — any progress is lost.
queue.dashboard_warning_recovery_required: Queue data needs recovery — go to Settings → Queue Management to review it.
queue.dashboard_warning_degraded: Queue state is not currently durable — automatic retry in progress. New dispatches are paused until this clears.
queue.dashboard_warning_stopped_by_admin: Queue automation was manually stopped for every printer — resume it from Settings → Queue Management.

notif.enable_desc: Push alerts about your fleet, sent by a background watcher independent of whether the dashboard is open.

notif.events_desc: Which print state changes send a notification.
notif.milestones_desc: Notify when a print crosses chosen progress percentages
notif.milestone_hint_none: No percentages selected — pick at least one below, or the switch above has nothing to send.
notif.providers_desc: Either, both, or neither can be on at once.
notif.topic_warn: The topic acts as a shared secret — anyone who knows it receives your notifications. Regenerating stops delivery to anyone already subscribed to the old one.
notif.regenerate_confirm: Regenerate the ntfy topic? Anyone already subscribed to the current one will stop receiving notifications.
notif.chat_id_help: A leading minus means a group chat; a plain positive number is a direct message.
notif.test_error_missing_chat_id: Enter a Telegram chat ID first
notif.test_error_missing_bot_token: Enter a Telegram bot token first
notif.test_error_invalid_topic: Enter a valid ntfy topic first
notif.webhook_url_warn: The URL is a secret — anyone who has it can post to your channel. http and https only, and redirects are never followed.
notif.webhook_format_help: Discord sends a rich embed with the camera snapshot. Generic JSON sends SnapCon's own fields for tools like n8n or Home Assistant.

printers.remove_confirm: Remove "{name}"? This won't take effect until you save.

printers.field_tags_hint: comma-separated — e.g. filter Camera View, or /red/ to tint the card

printers.force_defaults_desc: Print always uses the defaults below with no prompt. Turn off to confirm Auto-level / Flow Calibration / Time-lapse (and which toolheads to calibrate, on U1) before each print instead.
printers.auto_level_desc: Home and probe the bed mesh before each print
printers.flow_cal_desc: Run a flow-rate calibration pass before each print
printers.timelapse_desc: Capture a time-lapse video of each print
printers.defaults_hint: These are just the defaults — Print and Send-to-Printers both let you override them per job.

printers.access_hint: Which groups can see and use this printer — default: Everyone.
printers.no_groups_yet: No groups yet — add one from the Users tab.

printers.pool_error_queue_not_idle: This printer's queue must be idle before changing its pool
printers.pool_error_queue_not_empty: Clear this printer's queue before changing its pool
printers.pool_error_monitor_only: This printer is monitored only — SnapCon cannot send it prints, so it cannot join a Printer Pool.
printers.discover_scope_hint_local: Scans every subnet this SnapCon host is connected to.
printers.discover_scope_hint_subnet: Scan one subnet you specify — e.g. 192.168.2.0, or CIDR like 192.168.22.128/25.
printers.discover_none_found: No printers found on {subnets}. Add manually instead.
printers.discover_needs_update: This needs the updated server.js — replace it and restart the hub.
printers.transport_hint: Stock firmware serves the FlashForge API on port 8898. A firmware mod such as ZMOD or Forge-X replaces it with Moonraker on port 7125. SnapCon normally detects which is live and re-checks if it changes — pin a specific one only if detection gets it wrong.
printers.monitor_only_hint: Monitoring only: SnapCon reads status, progress, temperatures and AMS slots over the printer's local connection and never sends it commands. Enter the printer's serial number and its 8-character LAN access code (on the printer: Settings → Network / LAN Only Mode). LAN Only Mode itself does not need to be switched on. For the camera, switch on "LAN Only Liveview" on the printer; for job previews, turn on "Store sent files on external storage" with a USB drive or SD card inserted.

firmware.pick_no_folder: Set a firmware folder first, in Settings → General.
firmware.pick_failed: Could not read the firmware folder.
firmware.confirm_consequence_offline: The printer goes offline for several minutes while it writes the image.
firmware.confirm_consequence_power: Do not cut power or unplug it until it comes back.
firmware.confirm_consequence_one: Printers are updated one at a time, not all at once.
firmware.skip_current_label: Skip printers already on this version
firmware.skip_current_desc: Avoids re-sending a quarter-gigabyte image to a printer that already runs it. Turn off to reinstall the same version.
firmware.ineligible_printing: Printing — stop the print before updating firmware
firmware.ineligible_offline: Offline — SnapCon cannot reach this printer
firmware.ineligible_unsupported: This printer's connector does not support firmware updates
firmware.row_flash: Writing firmware — do not cut power
firmware.confirm_version_unknown: Version could not be read from the image
firmware.ineligible_in_progress: A firmware update is already running on this printer
firmware.confirm_skip_no_version: This image does not state its version, so no printer will be skipped — every selected printer will be updated.
firmware.inspect_http_error: The firmware file could not be checked (HTTP {status}). If SnapCon was updated, restart the server.
firmware.verify_desc: Has the printer check the image it received against the local file before writing it. Costs about 15 seconds and almost no network traffic. Turning this off flashes whatever arrived, unchecked — a corrupted image can leave a printer unbootable.
firmware.confirm_no_verify: Verification is off. Nothing will check that the image arrived intact before it is written.
firmware.row_refresh_failed: Updated — could not re-read the version
firmware.image_none_help: Choose an image to see which printers need it. Your printers' current versions are listed below either way.
firmware.image_version_unknown: Version not stated in the image
firmware.group_select_all: Select every printer in this group
firmware.row_mcu_mismatch: One board is on a different version — it missed an update

remote_access.enable_desc: Get a public HTTPS address for this SnapCon, tunnelled through Cloudflare.
remote_access.enable_desc_gated: Requires User Access Management with at least one admin account.
remote_access.insecure_warning: ⚠ The tunnel token is stored in an INSECURE local file fallback (no OS credential store was available). This is not real secure storage.
remote_access.gate_title: Turn on User Access Management first
remote_access.gate_body: A public address with no login lets anyone who has the link start prints and heat beds. Turn on User Access Management and create at least one account before enabling Remote Access.
remote_access.off_line: Off. No tunnel running, public address not reachable.
remote_access.verification_needed_desc: One-time step: open this link and complete the verification challenge in your browser to finish setting up this device.
remote_access.who_can_sign_in_desc: Anyone signing in through the public address uses one of these accounts.
remote_access.disable_confirm: Disable Remote Access? This stops remote access immediately. The tunnel identity is kept so re-enabling doesn't require setting it up again.
remote_access.remove_confirm: Remove Remote Access? This permanently deletes this device's remote Hub. You will need to complete the verification step again to re-enable it. This cannot be undone.
remote_access.copy_failed: Could not copy — copy the URL manually
remote_access.error_users_disabled: SnapCon login protection (User Access Management) is not enabled. Enable it in Settings → Users first.

logs.unavailable: Audit logging isn't available on this server (needs Node 22.5+)

queue.enable_desc: Ordered per-printer queues, with a defined way to handle the gap between prints
